case_slice: G05.var02 NBREQ boundary with one passive standby

parent.acceptance: accepted fixed-seed B-to-A-to-C passive standby with half-hour TSWOV

model.repair: unchanged half-hour direct system CM after return

manual_observation: Installed SIMLOX manual physical pp197-200,455-458: a parallel block works when operated branches >= NBREQ, is in SWITCHOVER when operated plus activating branches >= NBREQ, and is nonfunctional otherwise. NBOP=2<3 creates one passive branch. The manual states activated-branch failure generation starts on switch finish at p199 but on initiation at p456; this pair does not predecide that conflict.
hypotheses_to_test_natively: Both arms import/export/convert with zero errors and preserve exactly the intended NBOP=2/NBREQ delta.
Native events identify the initially operated positions and the standby selected after the first operated-position failure; PRIO alone is insufficient to assert initial selection.
With NBREQ=1, one surviving operated branch may keep the system working through the first standby activation; the report should distinguish branch switchover from system SWITCHOVER.
With NBREQ=2, a first operated-branch failure may put the system in SWITCHOVER while the standby activates; a later loss below NBREQ without a spare may make it unavailable and alter mission outcome.
All failure samples, mission transitions, deferred CM and 72-bin System/Stock metrics must be recorded separately; matching random draws or event times are not preaccepted.
acceptance_gates: frozen parent/source hashes, exact table delta, installed manual/dictionary/executable hashes
session-0 SSH with sshd ancestor, host-wide native mutex, preserved GUI PID 13340, unique run directories
native import/export/calc/report and exact authored-row roundtrip with zero converter errors
event-level branch, state, mission, repair and report reconciliation by author and independent read-only reviewer
raw invocation, logs, model, report and closure SHA-256 seals in evidence index
limits: One fixed seed and one repetition cannot establish population reliability or all priority permutations.

POS-C has no failure mode; unavailable preferred standby, simultaneous failures, overlapping switches, nested propagation, online repair, GUI RBD rendering and cross-engine parity remain separate cases.
